Lebanon.wildlife_intro:
Lebanon's calls run city-classic: Norway rats in the older row-home and industrial blocks, raccoons in chimneys across the North and South sides, squirrels in the township street trees, and bats in the attics of the older stock. The Quittapahilla corridor carries skunks through the city.

The Lebanon year runs in waves. Cold months drive squirrels and rodents into attics, and big brown bats overwinter quietly in wall voids across the older housing. Spring opens raccoon denning season and groundhog digging, summer brings bat maternity colonies — Pennsylvania Game Commission guidance treats May 15 through August 1 as the window when exclusions should wait — and fall sends a second wave of squirrels and rodents looking for winter rooms. Our crew starts with a full inspection, then removes the animals and seals every entry we find, because closing only the obvious hole rarely holds. Attached housing dominates the core; our crew maps connected rooflines before quoting sealing.
